items.label: Explain how two changing quantities are connected in a graph

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: generate tables of values from visually growing patterns or the rule of a function; describe and plot these relationships on the Cartesian plane
items.label: Turn a pattern or rule into a table and graph

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: manipulate formulas involving several variables using digital tools, and describe the effect of systematic variation in the values of the variables
items.label: Explore how changing values in a formula changes the result

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: solve problems involving the area of triangles and parallelograms using established formulas and appropriate units
items.label: Calculate the area of triangles and parallelograms

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: solve problems involving the volume of right prisms including rectangular and triangular prisms, using established formulas and appropriate units
items.label: Calculate the volume of box-shaped and triangular prisms

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: describe the relationship between \(π\) and the features of circles including the circumference, radius and diameter
items.label: Connect a circle’s radius, diameter and distance around it using pi

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: identify corresponding, alternate and co-interior relationships between angles formed when parallel lines are crossed by a transversal; use them to solve problems and explain reasons
items.label: Find angles where a line crosses parallel lines

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: demonstrate that the interior angle sum of a triangle in the plane is 180° and apply this to determine the interior angle sum of other shapes and the size of unknown angles
items.label: Use the angle totals of triangles and other shapes

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving ratios; formulate problems, interpret and communicate solutions in terms of the situation, justifying choices made about the representation
items.label: Use ratios to solve practical measuring problems

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: represent objects in 2 dimensions; discuss and reason about the advantages and disadvantages of different representations
items.label: Show a 3D object in 2D and compare different views

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: classify triangles, quadrilaterals and other polygons according to their side and angle properties; identify and reason about relationships
items.label: Sort triangles and other polygons by sides and angles

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: describe transformations of a set of points using coordinates in the Cartesian plane, translations and reflections on an axis, and rotations about a given point
items.label: Use coordinates to slide, flip or turn a shape

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: design and create algorithms involving a sequence of steps and decisions that will sort and classify sets of shapes according to their attributes, and describe how the algorithms work
items.label: Create step-by-step rules for sorting shapes

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: acquire data sets for discrete and continuous numerical variables and calculate the range, median, mean and mode; make and justify decisions about which measures of central tendency provide useful insights into the nature of the distribution of data
items.label: Choose useful averages and calculate mean, median, mode and range

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: create different types of numerical data displays including stem-and-leaf plots using software where appropriate; describe and compare the distribution of data, commenting on the shape, centre and spread including outliers and determining the range, median, mean and mode
items.label: Compare data displays, including stem-and-leaf plots

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: plan and conduct statistical investigations involving data for discrete and continuous numerical variables; analyse and interpret distributions of data and report findings in terms of shape and summary statistics
items.label: Investigate numerical data and explain its centre, spread and shape

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: identify the sample space for single-stage events; assign probabilities to the outcomes of these events and predict relative frequencies for related events
items.label: List possible outcomes and work out their probabilities

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: conduct repeated chance experiments and run simulations with a large number of trials using digital tools; compare predictions about outcomes with observed results, explaining the differences
items.label: Compare predicted chance results with many repeated trials

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: recognise irrational numbers in applied contexts, including square roots and \(π\)
items.label: Understand numbers such as pi and square roots that are not exact fractions

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: establish and apply the exponent laws with positive integer exponents and the zero-exponent, using exponent notation with numbers
items.label: Use rules for powers, including a power of zero

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: recognise terminating and recurring decimals, using digital tools as appropriate
items.label: Recognise decimals that stop or repeat

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: use the 4 operations with integers and with rational numbers, choosing and using efficient strategies and digital tools where appropriate
items.label: Calculate with negative numbers, fractions and decimals

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving rational numbers and percentages, including financial contexts; formulate problems, choosing efficient calculation strategies and using digital tools where appropriate; interpret and communicate solutions in terms of the situation, reviewing the appropriateness of the model
items.label: Use fractions and percentages to solve practical and money problems

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: create, expand, factorise, rearrange and simplify linear expressions, applying the associative, commutative, identity, distributive and inverse properties
items.label: Expand brackets, collect matching terms and simplify expressions

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: graph linear relations on the Cartesian plane using digital tools where appropriate; solve linear equations and one-variable inequalities using graphical and algebraic techniques; verify solutions by substitution
items.label: Solve straight-line equations and inequalities using algebra or graphs

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: use mathematical modelling to solve applied problems  involving linear relations, including financial contexts; formulate problems with linear functions, choosing a representation; interpret and communicate solutions in terms of the situation, reviewing the appropriateness of the model
items.label: Use a straight-line rule to model an everyday situation

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: experiment with linear functions and relations using digital tools, making and testing conjectures and generalising emerging patterns
items.label: Explore how changing a straight-line rule changes its graph

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: solve problems involving the area and perimeter of irregular and composite shapes using appropriate units
items.label: Find the area and perimeter of shapes made from simpler parts

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: solve problems involving the volume and capacity of right prisms using appropriate units
items.label: Calculate a prism’s volume and how much it holds

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: solve problems involving the circumference and area of a circle using formulas and appropriate units
items.label: Calculate the area and distance around a circle

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: solve problems involving duration, including using 12- and 24-hour time across multiple time zones
items.label: Calculate times and durations across time zones

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: recognise and use rates to solve problems involving the comparison of 2 related quantities of different units of measure
items.label: Compare rates such as kilometres per hour or dollars per kilogram

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: use Pythagoras’ theorem to solve problems involving the side lengths of right-angled triangles
items.label: Use Pythagoras’ rule to find a side of a right-angled triangle

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving ratios and rates, including financial contexts; formulate problems; interpret and communicate solutions in terms of the situation, reviewing the appropriateness of the model
items.label: Use ratios and rates to solve practical problems

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: identify the conditions for congruence and similarity of triangles and explain the conditions for other sets of common shapes to be congruent or similar, including those formed by transformations
items.label: Decide whether shapes are identical or scaled copies

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: establish properties of quadrilaterals using congruent triangles and angle properties, and solve related problems explaining reasoning
items.label: Use triangle and angle facts to explain properties of four-sided shapes

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: describe the position and location of objects in 3 dimensions in different ways, including using a three-dimensional coordinate system with the use of dynamic geometric software and other digital tools
items.label: Describe a position using three coordinates

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: design, create and test algorithms involving a sequence of steps and decisions that identify congruency or similarity of shapes, and describe how the algorithm works
items.label: Create and test rules for identifying matching or scaled shapes

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: investigate techniques for data collection including census, sampling, experiment and observation, and explain the practicalities and implications of obtaining data through these techniques
items.label: Choose between surveys, samples, observations and experiments

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: analyse and report on the distribution of data from primary and secondary sources using random and non-random sampling techniques to select and study samples
items.label: Explain how the way a sample is chosen affects results

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: compare variations in distributions and proportions obtained from random samples of the same size drawn from a population and recognise the effect of sample size on this variation
items.label: Explore how sample size affects variation in results

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: plan and conduct statistical investigations involving samples of a population; use ethical and fair methods to make inferences about the population and report findings, acknowledging uncertainty
items.label: Use a fair sample to draw cautious conclusions about a larger group

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: recognise that complementary events have a combined probability of one; use this relationship to calculate probabilities in applied contexts
items.label: Use the chance of something not happening to find its chance of happening

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: determine all possible combinations for 2 events, using two-way tables, tree diagrams and Venn diagrams, and use these to determine probabilities of specific outcomes in practical situations
items.label: List two-event combinations with tables, trees or Venn diagrams

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: conduct repeated chance experiments and simulations, using digital tools to determine probabilities for compound events, and describe results
items.label: Use repeated experiments to explore the chance of combined events

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: recognise that the real number system includes the rational numbers and the irrational numbers, and solve problems involving real numbers using digital tools
items.label: Work with fractions, decimals, square roots and other real numbers

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: apply the exponent laws to numerical expressions with integer exponents and extend to variables
items.label: Use power rules with negative powers and letters

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: simplify algebraic expressions, expand binomial products and factorise monic quadratic expressions
items.label: Expand two brackets and factorise simple quadratic expressions

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: find the gradient of a line segment, the midpoint of the line interval and the distance between 2 distinct points on the Cartesian plane
items.label: Find a line’s slope, a midpoint and the distance between two points

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: identify and graph quadratic functions, solve quadratic equations graphically and numerically, and solve monic quadratic equations with integer roots algebraically, using graphing software and digital tools as appropriate
items.label: Graph a quadratic curve and solve its equation

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: use mathematical modelling to solve applied problems involving change including financial contexts; formulate problems, choosing to use either linear or quadratic functions; interpret solutions in terms of the situation; evaluate the model and report methods and findings
items.label: Choose a straight-line or curved model for change in a real situation

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: experiment with the effects of the variation of parameters on graphs of related functions, using digital tools, making connections between graphical and algebraic representations, and generalising emerging patterns
items.label: Explain how changing an equation changes its graph

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: solve problems involving the volume and surface area of right prisms and cylinders using appropriate units
items.label: Calculate the surface area and volume of prisms and cylinders

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: solve problems involving very small and very large measurements, time scales and intervals expressed in scientific notation
items.label: Use scientific notation for very large or tiny measurements

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: solve spatial problems, applying angle properties, scale, similarity, Pythagoras’ theorem and trigonometry in right-angled triangles
items.label: Use triangle, angle and scale rules to solve spatial problems

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: calculate and interpret absolute, relative and percentage errors in measurements, recognising that all measurements are estimates
items.label: Calculate the size and percentage of a measurement error

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving direct proportion, rates, ratio and scale, including financial contexts; formulate the problems and interpret solutions in terms of the situation; evaluate the model and report methods and findings
items.label: Use proportion, rates and scale to solve practical problems

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: recognise the constancy of the sine, cosine and tangent ratios for a given angle in right-angled triangles using properties of similarity
items.label: Understand sine, cosine and tangent using right-angled triangles

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: apply the enlargement transformation to shapes and objects using dynamic geometry software as appropriate; identify and explain aspects that remain the same and those that change
items.label: Enlarge shapes and explain what changes and what stays the same

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: design, test and refine algorithms involving a sequence of steps and decisions based on geometric constructions and theorems; discuss and evaluate refinements
items.label: Test and improve step-by-step methods for geometry problems

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: analyse reports of surveys in digital media and elsewhere for information on how data was obtained to estimate population means and medians
items.label: Check how a survey was used to estimate an average

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: analyse how different sampling methods can affect the results of surveys and how choice of representation can be used to support a particular point of view
items.label: Spot how sampling or charts can favour one point of view

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: represent the distribution of multiple data sets for numerical variables using comparative representations; compare data distributions with consideration of centre, spread and shape, and the effect of outliers on these measures
items.label: Compare groups of data and the effect of unusual values

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: choose appropriate forms of display or visualisation for a given type of data; justify selections and interpret displays for a given context
items.label: Choose a suitable chart and explain why it fits the data

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: plan and conduct statistical investigations involving the collection and analysis of different kinds of data; report findings and discuss the strength of evidence to support any conclusions
items.label: Investigate data and explain how strongly it supports a conclusion

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: list all outcomes for compound events both with and without replacement, using lists, tree diagrams, tables or arrays; assign probabilities to outcomes
items.label: Work out combined chances with and without replacing an item

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: calculate relative frequencies from given or collected data to estimate probabilities of events involving “and”, inclusive “or” and exclusive “or”
items.label: Use data to estimate chances involving and or or

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: design and conduct repeated chance experiments and simulations, using digital tools to compare probabilities of simple events to related compound events, and describe results
items.label: Compare the chance of a single event with combined events

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: recognise the effect of using approximations of real numbers in repeated calculations and compare the results when using exact representations
items.label: Explain how rounding repeatedly changes the final answer

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: expand, factorise and simplify expressions and solve equations algebraically, applying exponent laws involving products, quotients and powers of variables, and the distributive property
items.label: Simplify expressions and solve equations using power and bracket rules

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: solve linear inequalities and simultaneous linear equations in 2 variables; interpret solutions graphically and communicate solutions in terms of the situation
items.label: Solve inequalities and pairs of simultaneous linear equations

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: recognise the connection between algebraic and graphical representations of exponential relations and solve related exponential equations, using digital tools where appropriate
items.label: Connect exponential graphs to equations and solve for an unknown

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: use mathematical modelling to solve applied problems involving growth and decay, including financial contexts; formulate problems, choosing to apply linear, quadratic or exponential models; interpret solutions in terms of the situation; evaluate and modify models as necessary and report assumptions, methods and findings
items.label: Model growth or decay and check how well the model fits

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: experiment with functions and relations using digital tools, making and testing conjectures and generalising emerging patterns
items.label: Use graphs and calculations to test a rule about functions

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: solve problems involving the surface area and volume of composite objects using appropriate units
items.label: Find the surface area and volume of joined 3D objects

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: interpret and use logarithmic scales  in applied contexts involving small and large quantities and change
items.label: Read scales where each equal step means multiplying, such as logarithmic scales

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: solve practical problems applying Pythagoras’ theorem and trigonometry of right-angled triangles, including problems involving direction and angles of elevation and depression
items.label: Use right-angled triangles to solve height and direction problems

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: identify the impact of measurement errors on the accuracy of results in practical contexts
items.label: Explain how measurement errors affect the final result

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving proportion and scaling of objects; formulate problems and interpret solutions in terms of the situation; evaluate and modify models as necessary, and report assumptions, methods and findings
items.label: Model how changing scale affects an object’s measurements

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: apply deductive reasoning to proofs involving shapes in the plane and use theorems to solve spatial problems
items.label: Build a logical proof about shapes using known facts

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: interpret networks and network diagrams used to represent relationships in practical situations and describe connectedness
items.label: Read network diagrams and explain how things are connected

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: design, test and refine solutions to spatial problems using algorithms and digital tools; communicate and justify solutions
items.label: Test and improve step-by-step solutions to spatial problems

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: analyse claims, inferences and conclusions of statistical reports in the media, including ethical considerations and identification of potential sources of bias
items.label: Check news reports for bias and unsupported statistical claims

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: compare data distributions for continuous numerical variables using appropriate data displays including boxplots; discuss the shapes of these distributions in terms of centre, spread, shape and outliers in the context of the data
items.label: Compare data distributions using boxplots and other displays

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: construct scatterplots and comment on the association between the 2 numerical variables in terms of strength, direction and linearity
items.label: Use a scatterplot to describe the relationship between two measurements

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: construct two-way tables and discuss possible relationship between categorical variables
items.label: Use a two-way table to explore links between categories

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: plan and conduct statistical investigations of situations that involve bivariate data; evaluate and report findings with consideration of limitations of any inferences
items.label: Investigate two related variables and explain limits to the conclusions

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: use the language of “if ... then”, “given”, “of”, “knowing that” to describe and interpret situations involving conditional probability
items.label: Work out how knowing one event happened changes another event’s chance

items.subject: Mathematics
items.description: design and conduct repeated chance experiments and simulations using digital tools to model conditional probability and interpret results
items.label: Use repeated experiments to explore chances when a condition is known
